What associations ask about membership modeling

Do we need member research first?

What is the difference between member types and tiers?

Member types charge different rates for substantially the same benefits. In individual membership associations, types usually follow career stage, such as student, early career and retired. In trade associations, they usually follow a member company's annual revenue. Tiers charge different rates for substantially different benefits.

What is a firm or group membership model?

One organization pays for a group of its people to join, instead of each person joining alone. We model how a group rate affects members, revenue and renewals.

How do associations grow membership?

By pulling three levers together: the benefits members value, dues rates set against peers, and member types or tiers that fit each audience. Recruitment offers, such as intro rates for students and young professionals, help too. Ricochet models each option in a working financial model, so you see the effect on members and revenue before you commit.

What causes member retention to drop?

First-year members are usually the weak spot. In the 2026 MGI Membership Marketing Benchmarking Report, first-year retention averages 61% at individual associations, against 79% overall. Weak onboarding, dues out of line with perceived value and benefits that miss key segments all add to it. A membership model shows which lever moves your renewal rate most.

How often should an association raise dues?

Many associations raise dues a little every year, tied to an inflation measure such as the Consumer Price Index. Larger increases have no set schedule. The right time is when the model shows an increase will grow revenue without losing more members than you can afford.

How do associations raise dues without losing members?

Model the increase before you decide. About half of associations raised dues in 2025: 49% of individual and 53% of trade associations, according to the 2026 MGI Membership Marketing Benchmarking Report.
